Michigan's one statutory repair escrow is in the Housing Law of Michigan and applies only where that law applies (edu-housing-law-mi): while a certificate of compliance has not been issued or has been suspended, the duty to pay rent is suspended and the rent is paid into an escrow account set up by the enforcing agency, to be paid out to you or another party authorized to make repairs, to cover the cost of correcting the violations. It applies whatever the size of your holdings. It has only two exceptions: it does not apply until you have had a reasonable time after notice of violations to apply for a temporary certificate, and it does not apply where you establish that the occupants caused the hazardous conditions. If the tenant does not pay the suspended rent into escrow, you may sue for rent and possession, subject to the tenant's defenses; rent paid into that escrow is a defense to an eviction for nonpayment (edu-tenant-repair-remedies-mi). A court may also order rent paid into court during an eviction (edu-rent-into-court-counterclaim-mi). The only small-landlord exemption in Michigan's landlord-tenant statutes is the source-of-income rule's exemption for landlords of fewer than 5 rental units (edu-source-of-income-mi), which has nothing to do with escrow or repairs.

title: No Designated Repairer Rule
bodyText:
No Michigan statute requires you to name a repair person or contractor, limits whom you may name, or says who must make the repairs that are yours. Where the Housing Law of Michigan applies, a multiple dwelling housing more than 8 families in which the owner does not live must have a responsible person designated by the owner; that is a supervision and safety rule, not a rule about repairers.

A tenant has no general statutory right to repair at your expense. In a Housing Law enforcement action a court may let an occupant who did not cause a violation correct it and deduct the cost from rent on terms the court sets, and when a court awards repair costs for your failure to repair, it compensates the tenant's own labor at a reasonable rate. Whether Michigan common law lets a tenant repair and deduct outside those statutes is case law.

So the lease may tell the tenant where to report repairs and require your written consent, naming who will do the work, before the tenant makes or hires out a repair at your expense or deducts one from rent, as long as it takes away no remedy the tenant has when the home is unfit (designated-repairer-mi). State licensing of building trades may limit who may do some work for pay; the library has not analysed it.

title: Rent Paid Into Court and Counterclaims
bodyText: In a Michigan eviction (summary proceedings) the tenant does not have to pay rent into court to raise a defense or a counterclaim, and counterclaims are optional (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts, administrative rules and the Michigan Court Rules searched). Rent into court: if the trial is adjourned more than 14 days and you show a clear need for protection, the court may order the tenant to pay a reasonable rent, set with the condition of the premises in mind, to the court clerk within 7 days and then within 7 days of each date rent would be due, until possession is decided. A tenant who does not pay waives a jury trial on possession only, and you are entitled to a trial within 14 days. Only the court may release the money, it must consider the tenant's defenses, and if the trial was postponed so that repairs could be made it may require the repairs to be finished first. A court may adjourn a trial for up to 56 days for good cause, so a long adjournment is when such an order is most likely. Counterclaims: either side may join money claims for damage to the premises, breach of the lease or wrongful possession, and the tenant's money counterclaim must be labeled and separately stated in a written answer. A counterclaim that would change what the tenant must pay to stop the eviction must be tried with the possession claim unless it appears to have no merit; otherwise the court may try possession first. A possession judgment does not bar other claims, so a tenant who does not counterclaim may still sue later. Whatever the claims, in a nonpayment case the court deducts rent excused by your breach of the lease or of the covenants of fitness and repair. Where the Housing Law applies, rent paid into a Housing Law escrow, under a court repair order or to a receiver is a defense to eviction for nonpayment (edu-no-repair-escrow-exemption-notice-mi). See edu-eviction-process-mi for the rest of the procedure.

title: No Shutdown Rent Protection
bodyText: No Michigan statute gives a tenant extra time to pay rent, protection from late fees, or a stay of eviction because a federal, state or local government shutdown has interrupted the tenant's pay (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts and the administrative rules in the library's corpus searched). Rent is due when the lease says, and nonpayment follows the ordinary 7-day demand for possession (edu-nonpayment-notice-mi) and the court process, including the stay of a nonpayment case while a timely rental assistance application is pending, for up to 28 days (edu-eviction-process-mi). Federal servicemember protections are separate and not tied to a shutdown (edu-no-servicemember-statute-mi). You may agree with a furloughed tenant to defer rent. Because a lease may be changed after it begins only with the tenant's written consent, put the arrangement in a writing you both sign, stating the deferred amount, the dates it will be repaid and whether any late fee is waived. Write it as past-due rent repaid on those dates, not as a higher rent for later months: Michigan counts any rent required in a rental period above the average rent for the term as a security deposit, which is capped and must be handled under the deposit law.

title: Subsidies When Rent Is Reduced for Condition
bodyText: No Michigan statute says how a housing subsidy figures in when rent is reduced, excused or paid into escrow because of a unit's condition, or limits a tenant's reduction to the tenant's own share (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts and the administrative rules in the library's corpus searched). Michigan's condition-based rent rules do not mention subsidies: in an eviction for nonpayment the court deducts rent excused by your breach of the lease or of the covenants of fitness and repair, and where the Housing Law of Michigan applies, rent is suspended and paid into escrow while a certificate of compliance is withheld or suspended (edu-tenant-repair-remedies-mi). How those rules reach the part of the rent an agency pays is not settled by statute, and the library has not read case law on it. Michigan has one subsidy-specific rule. If you take part in the Department of Health and Human Services rent vendoring program, which the Housing Law ties to family independence program recipients, you certify that the unit is fit for human habitation, has no condition that would spread a communicable disease, and is not dangerous to life or health because of disrepair or a defect in drainage, plumbing, lighting, ventilation or heating. When an enforcing agency reports a code violation that is a hazard to the occupants' health or safety, the department ends your participation for that unit until it is corrected, and a Housing Law enforcing agency must report a serious and imminent hazard to the department within 48 hours. You may not evict an occupant based solely on that termination; an occupant evicted in violation may recover treble damages, costs and reasonable attorney fees. For a federal Housing Choice Voucher tenancy, federal rules cover the subsidy side. The family is not responsible for the part of the rent the housing assistance payment covers, and the housing authority's failure to pay is not a lease violation or a ground to end the tenancy. Once the authority notifies you in writing of deficiencies it may withhold its payments, and it must abate them if you do not fix a life-threatening deficiency within 24 hours or another deficiency within 30 days or an approved extension; you may not end the tenancy because of the withholding or abatement, and abated payments are not made up later. If the family, a household member or a guest caused the deficiency, the authority may waive your duty to fix it, and then may neither withhold nor abate. Do not bill the tenant for an abated or withheld assistance payment.

title: No Subsidized-Inspection Statute
bodyText: No Michigan statute deals with inspections of a voucher or other subsidized unit by the agency that pays the subsidy: nothing makes a tenant admit that agency's inspector, gives you a remedy when a subsidized tenant refuses one, or addresses a landlord who refuses the program's inspection (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts and the administrative rules in the library's corpus searched). Two state rules touch the subject. First, a landlord of 5 or more rental units in Michigan may not deny or end a tenancy, or set different terms, because of a tenant's source of income, which includes housing choice vouchers (edu-source-of-income-mi). Assistance the agency does not approve within 30 days after you provide all the information it requires for approval, including evidence that all repairs required before occupancy have been completed, is not protected source of income, so that period runs only once you have done what the program asks. Refusing the program's inspection or its required repairs in order to avoid a voucher tenant risks a source-of-income claim; whether a refusal of the inspection is itself a denial based on source of income is not settled by statute, and the library has not read case law on it. Second, where the Housing Law of Michigan applies (edu-housing-law-mi), the local enforcing agency may accept a HUD inspection in place of its own; its inspectors need the tenant's consent unless the lease authorizes inspector entry (housing-inspection-entry-mi), the tenant complained, the unit is vacant or a warrant issues; and if a tenant who refused the enforcing agency's inspection moves out before it happens, you must tell the agency within 10 days. Those rules govern the local housing inspector, not a housing authority's program inspection. Under the federal voucher rules you must keep the unit to the program's housing quality standards, and the unit fails them when an authorized inspector finds deficiencies on inspection, notifies you in writing and they are not corrected in time. Under the federal voucher rules the housing authority must inspect the unit before the initial lease term and at least every 2 years (every 3 for a small rural housing authority), and the family must allow the authority to inspect at reasonable times after reasonable notice; a family's refusal is a matter between the family and the authority under the program rules. The library offers no lease clause on program inspections: the voucher's own tenancy addendum supplies the program's terms, and a term imposed only on tenants with a voucher could itself be a distinction in lease terms based on source of income.

title: No Duty to Provide Alternate Housing
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a private landlord to provide or pay for alternate, temporary or substitute housing for a tenant, whether during repairs, after a fire or flood, or when a unit is unfit or ordered vacated, and no statute lets a tenant trigger such a duty by request (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts and the administrative rules in the library's corpus searched). What a tenant has instead: if the building is destroyed or made untenantable without the tenant's fault or neglect, the tenant may quit and surrender possession and owes no rent after surrender, unless the parties agreed otherwise in writing (edu-casualty-mi). Where the Housing Law of Michigan applies, the enforcing agency may order a unit vacated while a certificate of compliance is withheld or suspended; rent is then suspended and paid into escrow for repairs, and the agency returns any unspent escrow for the unexpired rental period if the occupant ends the tenancy before repairs are undertaken. In an eviction for nonpayment the court deducts rent excused by your breach, and an occupant may recover actual damages for unsafe, unsanitary or unhealthful conditions you fail to correct after notice (edu-tenant-repair-remedies-mi). Michigan's relocation-assistance laws bind state agencies and other public bodies that acquire property or displace residents for a public program (including urban renewal and highway work), not a private landlord renting its own units. For a federal Housing Choice Voucher tenancy, when the housing authority ends the assistance contract because you did not correct deficiencies, it gives the family at least 90 days to find a new unit and may use withheld or abated assistance for the family's moving costs; that is the authority's job, not yours. You may offer temporary housing or a rent credit if you choose; put the terms in writing.

title: Building Facilities and Amenities
bodyText: Michigan has no general statute listing building facilities a landlord must provide or maintain, and no statute puts a duty on a landlord for an automatic garage door opener, a laundry room, a fitness room or a similar amenity (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts and the administrative rules in the library's corpus searched). What reaches facilities: your covenant that the premises and all common areas are fit for the use intended; the security deposit law, which treats grounds and other facilities or areas promised for the tenant's use as part of the rental unit; and, where the Housing Law of Michigan applies, the owner's duties to keep public halls in a multiple dwelling adequately lighted at all times and to provide covered garbage receptacles in a multiple dwelling (edu-housing-law-mi). Say in the lease which facilities you provide (services-utilities-provided-ks-oh, common-area-use). A lease may not let you change its terms after it begins without the tenant's written consent, apart from three listed adjustments on 30 days' written notice, so do not plan to withdraw a facility the lease promises by notice alone. Equipment laws reach some facilities whoever owns them. An elevator, including an escalator, dumbwaiter or incline lift, must be built, maintained and used to the state elevator code and needs a certificate of operation issued annually; an inspector may seal it out of service for an unsafe condition, for not having a current certificate or for not complying with a correction order, and violations carry fines and, for repeat offenses, possible jail time. The state elevator law does not apply in a city, village or township with comparable elevator inspection ordinances, and a residential stairway chairlift or platform lift is not an elevator under it. A swimming pool for an apartment complex is a public swimming pool unless it serves a 1-to-4-family dwelling or no more than 4 units: it needs a state construction permit and a license to operate, displayed on the premises (edu-pool-safety-mi). Boilers are covered in edu-heating-mi, and smoke and carbon monoxide alarms in edu-smoke-alarms-mi.

title: Tenant Duties Under Michigan Law
bodyText:
Michigan has no single list of tenant duties of the uniform-act kind; the tenant's statutory duties are scattered.

Where the Housing Law of Michigan applies: tenants are responsible for the cleanliness of the parts of the premises they occupy and control; in a single-family or 2-family dwelling the occupants must provide, keep clean and keep in place proper covered garbage receptacles; no horse, cow, swine, sheep, goat, chickens, geese or ducks may be kept in any dwelling; each occupant must comply with the provisions that apply specifically to the occupant; and a tenant must give the local enforcing agency access for an inspection during reasonable hours if the lease authorizes inspector entry, the tenant complained, the tenant consented or the agency serves a warrant.

Everywhere: your repair covenant does not cover disrepair or a health or safety violation caused by the tenant's wilful or irresponsible conduct or lack of conduct; if a tenant wilfully or negligently causes a serious and continuing health hazard or extensive and continuing physical injury to the premises, and you discovered it (or reasonably should have) no more than 90 days before you file, you may serve a 7-day demand to restore or repair the premises or deliver possession; and the security deposit covers actual damage from conduct not reasonably expected in normal living.

Under the security deposit law, the tenant reviews and returns the move-in inventory checklist within 7 days after taking possession (unless you agree on a shorter period) and must give you a forwarding address in writing within 4 days after moving out, failing which you are relieved of the notice of damages, though the tenant can still claim the deposit.

A tenant who takes occupancy must open a utility account within 30 business days unless the lease includes the service, and in homes built before November 6, 1974 the state residential code has the occupant of a rental unit test and clean smoke alarms periodically.

The library's lease puts the general duties in the shared maintenance and conduct clauses (tenant-maintenance, prohibited-acts-renter-mi) and offers an optional garbage-receptacle clause for single-family and 2-family homes (tenant-garbage-receptacles-mi).

title: What Michigan Habitability Law Does Not Cover
bodyText: Michigan's habitability law is short: the landlord's covenants of fitness and repair, which a lease may modify only with a current term of at least 1 year and whose remedies no lease may alter; the Housing Law of Michigan, only in the places it covers; and the eviction statutes that excuse rent for your breach. No section of the Michigan Compiled Laws or Constitution supplies any of the following (each searched for the row named): an indoor temperature or heating season standard (edu-heating-mi); a duty to supply a stove or refrigerator (edu-no-stove-refrigerator-rule-mi); a presumption that appliances at the home are supplied, or a rule on excluding them (appliances-excluded-mi); rules specific to furnished units (furnishings-included-mi; any deposit held for furnishings is a security deposit under the 1 1/2-month cap and the deposit act); any condition on shifting repairs to the tenant beyond the 1-year term, such as consideration or a separate writing (edu-maintenance-duty-shift-mi); a form, channel or written-notice rule for repair requests, or a notice condition on your repair duty (edu-repair-notice-mi); a right to end the lease or refuse a repair because it costs too much (edu-no-repair-cost-termination-mi); a small-landlord exemption from rent escrow or an exemption notice (edu-no-repair-escrow-exemption-notice-mi); a designated-repairer rule or a general tenant repair-and-deduct right outside a court order (edu-no-designated-repairer-rule-mi); a requirement that the tenant pay rent into court to raise a defense (edu-rent-into-court-counterclaim-mi); shutdown protection for government workers (edu-no-shutdown-rent-protection-mi); a rule on how a housing subsidy figures in a rent reduction (edu-subsidy-habitability-proration-mi) or on subsidized-unit inspections (edu-no-subsidized-inspection-refusal-rule-mi); a duty to provide alternate housing (edu-no-alt-housing-duty-mi); a duty for a garage door opener, laundry or other amenity (edu-other-landlord-facilities-mi); or a uniform list of tenant duties (edu-tenant-statutory-duties-mi). Earlier rows record more: no habitability presumption or required habitability statement (edu-no-habitability-presumption-mi, edu-no-habitability-statement-mi), no landlord right to fix a tenant's breach and bill it as rent (edu-no-landlord-self-cure-mi), no statutory covenant of quiet enjoyment (edu-no-quiet-possession-statute-mi), and no mold, bed bug or radon disclosure statute for leases (edu-no-mold-disclosure-mi, edu-no-bed-bug-rule-mi, edu-no-radon-disclosure-mi), though the Seller Disclosure Act's form, which asks about radon, mold and appliances such as a garage door opener, reaches a lease with an option to purchase a home of 1 to 4 units. Building codes adopted by reference, administrative rules not in the library's corpus and local ordinances (Detroit, Grand Rapids, Ann Arbor, Lansing and others) may add requirements.

title: Fire and Building Safety Codes
bodyText:
Michigan's fire safety rules for rental buildings come from three state sources, plus local codes.

(1) Fire Prevention Code: the state fire marshal's fire safety rules for operating and maintaining buildings cover apartment and other residential buildings, but not 1- and 2-family dwellings or mobile homes. The state fire marshal or a local fire chief may inspect any building for fire hazards (for example, missing or inadequate fire escapes, defective wiring, heating or gas connections, or accumulated rubbish) and the state fire marshal may order the owner to repair the building, change or end its use, or remove it; the owner gets at least 10 days to state in writing that it will comply with a repair order and at least 30 days to comply. Keeping a fire hazard in violation of the act or its rules is a misdemeanor.

(2) State construction code: it applies throughout the state to building, alteration, use and occupancy, and adopts the International Residential, Building, Existing Building (the Michigan Rehabilitation Code), Mechanical, Plumbing and Energy Codes and the National Electrical Code with Michigan amendments; your local building department or the state enforces it. Since July 21, 2026, a multiple-family dwelling of not more than 4 levels above grade may have a single interior exit stairway if it meets listed conditions, including a manual fire alarm system, automatic smoke detection and sprinklers in the stairway.

(3) Where the Housing Law of Michigan applies: fire escapes must be kept safe, sound, painted and free of obstructions; every part of a multiple dwelling above the first story needs 2 independent means of egress; no dwelling may be used to store dangerous or combustible articles except under a fire official's written permit; a multiple dwelling of more than 8 families whose owner does not live there must have a responsible person designated by the owner; employees of a multiple dwelling must be regularly instructed and drilled for fire and, in a fire, must call the fire department and help occupants leave; and class b buildings (hotels, rooming, lodging and boarding houses) keep a guest and tenant register and, above listed sizes, have watch, staffing and alarm duties.

An elevator must meet the state elevator safety standard and rules and needs a certificate of operation issued each year, and an inspector may seal it out of service, unless your city, village or township has a comparable elevator inspection ordinance.

Many cities adopt their own fire and property maintenance codes; this library does not cover local ordinances.

title: Fire Sprinklers
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires an owner to add fire sprinklers to an existing rental dwelling (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). Sprinkler requirements come from the state construction code when a building is built or altered. The state residential code for 1- and 2-family dwellings and townhouses leaves out the model code's sections that require sprinklers in those homes, so sprinklers there are optional; where they are installed they must meet the NFPA 13D standard or the plumbing code's sprinkler section. The state building code, which governs new apartment and other multifamily buildings, adopts the International Building Code's sprinkler rules with Michigan amendments; ask the building department what a particular building needs. Where the Housing Law of Michigan applies (see `edu-housing-law-mi`), older rooming, lodging and boarding houses (class b multiple dwellings) above set sizes that are not of fireproof construction and not protected by an approved sprinkler system or an approved automatic fire alarm system must keep a night watch, staff on duty or a manual alarm, and some basements must be protected by plaster, sprinklers or a fire alarm system. Only a firm certified by the state may install, modify, test, service or maintain a fire suppression system that the fire safety rules require, and test and maintenance records must be filed with the building owner. Some cities require more by ordinance.

title: No Sprinkler Disclosure Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to tell a tenant, in the lease or otherwise, whether the building has fire sprinklers, and no Michigan statute offers owners a grant, loan or tax credit for adding sprinklers to rental housing (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). Nothing needs to go in the lease. If you choose to describe the building's fire protection, describe it accurately. Sprinkler requirements themselves are in `edu-fire-sprinkler-duty-mi`. Some cities may require more by ordinance.

title: No Water Heater Temperature Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute or residential code rule tells a landlord what temperature to set a water heater at, or requires resetting it before a new tenant moves in (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts and the state residential code rules searched). Where the Housing Law of Michigan applies (see `edu-housing-law-mi`), each apartment or family unit must have at least 1 approved sink with running water furnished in sufficient quantity at all times, and the owner must provide the tanks, pumps or other equipment to supply it; your repair and habitability covenants (`edu-habitability-mi`) also cover a water heater you supply. Some cities set hot water temperatures in their property maintenance codes; this library does not cover local ordinances. Setting a tank water heater at a safe temperature at each turnover is a sensible practice, not a state rule.

title: No Window Guard Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to install window guards or other window-fall protection, to give a lease notice about them, or to regulate burglar or security bars on residential windows (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts and the state residential code rules searched). The state construction code adopts the model codes' rules on emergency escape windows and window-fall protection for new construction and alterations without a Michigan change, so check with the building department before you put bars, grilles or other covers over a sleeping-room window, which must still work as an escape route where the code requires one. Your repair and habitability covenants (`edu-habitability-mi`) cover windows and any guards you supply. Some cities may require more by ordinance.

title: No Steam Radiator Cover Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires covers or guards on steam radiators or a lease rider about them (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). Your repair and habitability covenants (`edu-habitability-mi`) cover heating equipment you supply. If a building is heated by a low-pressure steam boiler, the boiler must have a state certificate inspection every 2 years, unless it carries a pressure of not more than 15 pounds per square inch and is in a private residence or an apartment building with a capacity of fewer than 6 families. Some cities may require more by ordinance.

title: Pools at Rental Properties
bodyText:
A pool at an apartment complex, condominium, mobile home park or similar rental property is usually a public swimming pool under Michigan's Public Health Code. The act covers a pool used collectively by a number of people at an apartment, club, hotel, mobile home park, subdivision or similar premises, but not a pool on the same premises as a 1- to 4-family dwelling that is for the benefit of its occupants and their guests, and not a pool serving not more than 4 hotel, motel, apartment, condominium or similar units.

If your pool is covered, you need a state construction permit (with approved plans) before building or modifying it, and a license to operate it, displayed on the premises; the state or the local health department inspects it and may order it closed until it complies, and the department's swimming pool rules govern operation.

A pool for a single-family or 1- to 4-family rental is not a public swimming pool, but the state residential code's pool and spa provisions and your local building code still apply to building one.

No Michigan statute requires a pool safety notice in a lease. Your fitness covenant covers a pool that is a common area. Some cities add pool fencing and safety rules by ordinance. An optional pool and spa use clause is offered (`pool-and-spa-use-mi`).

title: No Security Device Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires deadbolts, door viewers, window locks or other security devices, or requires you to rekey locks between tenants (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). Three rules do apply. (1) Changing, altering or adding to the locks or other security devices without immediately giving the tenant keys or other unlocking devices, or removing doors, windows or locks, is unlawful interference with the tenant's possession; the tenant may recover actual damages or $200, whichever is greater, for each occurrence. This does not apply when you act under a court order, when you interfere only temporarily and only as needed for repairs or inspection as the law allows, when you believe in good faith after diligent inquiry that the tenant has abandoned the home and current rent is unpaid, or under the deceased-tenant procedure. (`edu-self-help-eviction-mi`). (2) Your repair and habitability covenants (`edu-habitability-mi`) cover the locks and doors you supply. (3) No Michigan statute gives a tenant, including a domestic violence victim, a right to change or add locks; a crime victim may be reimbursed by the state crime victim compensation program for up to $1,000 per residence for replacing or repairing windows or locks or adding locks. Rekeying between tenants is good practice. The library's `keys` and `lock-change-ak` clauses govern keys and lock changes; some cities set lock requirements by ordinance.

title: No Smart Access Law
bodyText:
No Michigan statute regulates smart locks or keypad, fob, card, app or biometric entry systems in rental housing, and no Michigan statute regulates a private landlord's collection of fingerprints, face scans or other biometric identifiers.

The general rules still apply. Changing, altering or adding to the locks or other security devices without immediately giving the tenant keys or other unlocking devices is unlawful interference with possession unless an exception applies (a court order, temporary repairs or inspection as the law allows, a good-faith belief, after diligent inquiry, that the tenant has abandoned the home and does not intend to return, with current rent unpaid, or the deceased-tenant procedure), so do not deactivate or reprogram a tenant's code, card, fob or app access during the tenancy without giving a working replacement at the same time.

A remote unlock is still an entry: where the Housing Law applies you must request and obtain the tenant's permission except in an emergency. An optional smart access clause is offered (`smart-access-system-mi`).

title: No Key Control Rule
bodyText:
No Michigan statute requires a landlord to adopt a key-control policy, to limit or log staff access to master keys, or to run background checks on employees who hold keys, and no Michigan statute gives a tenant, including a domestic violence victim, a right to change or add locks.

Keeping master keys and codes secure, logging who holds them and screening staff who have them are good practice.

Whatever your policy, you may not change the locks or other security devices without immediately giving the tenant keys or other unlocking devices, except under a court order, for temporary repairs or inspection as the law allows, when you believe in good faith, after diligent inquiry, that the tenant has abandoned the home and does not intend to return and current rent is unpaid, or under the deceased-tenant procedure, and entry with a master key follows the lease's entry clause and, where the Housing Law applies, its permission rule.

The library's `keys` clause governs the keys you issue, and the shared `lock-change-ak` clause, which applies in Michigan as written, requires the tenant to get your written agreement before changing a lock, except in an emergency.

title: Lighting of Halls and Common Areas
bodyText:
Where the Housing Law of Michigan applies, you must keep every public hall in a multiple dwelling adequately lighted at all times. In rooming, lodging and boarding houses (class b multiple dwellings), except larger fireproof ones, each floor must also have electrically lit exit signs, on a separate circuit, showing the stairways and means of egress; in multiple dwellings built before the act, the health officer may order more light and ventilation for public halls and stairs.

Everywhere, your fitness covenant covers the common areas. No Michigan statute or Public Service Commission rule addresses common-area lights wired to a tenant's own electric service. If yours are, say so in the lease and keep the duty to light and maintain the shared areas yourself; the shared `common-area-lighting-ks` clause, which applies in Michigan as written, does that. Some cities set lighting rules by ordinance.

title: No Balcony Inspection Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires periodic inspection of balconies, decks, stairways or other exterior elevated parts of rental buildings, or a report to tenants about them (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts and the state residential code rules searched). Your repair and habitability covenants (`edu-habitability-mi`) cover balconies and decks that are part of the premises or the common areas. Where the Housing Law of Michigan applies (see `edu-housing-law-mi`), balconies, porches, outside stairways and fire escapes count as part of the building, fire escapes must be kept in a safe and sound condition and properly painted and repaired, and the local enforcing agency may act against a dangerous building. Building, replacing or altering a deck or balcony, other than ordinary repairs, generally needs a building permit under the state construction code. Some cities require periodic inspections by ordinance.

title: Asbestos
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to inspect for asbestos or to tell tenants that a building contains it (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). The state rules apply when asbestos is disturbed. (1) A business that removes, encapsulates or demolishes friable asbestos materials on another's premises must be licensed by the state as an asbestos abatement contractor, so hire a licensed contractor (federal asbestos rules, not covered here, may also apply to your own staff); an electrical, mechanical or plumbing contractor or a licensed residential builder or maintenance and alteration contractor may handle a project incidental to its trade of not more than 160 square feet or 260 linear feet. (2) The contractor must notify the state in writing at least 10 days before a project involving more than 10 linear feet or 15 square feet of friable asbestos. (3) After a project of 10 linear feet or 15 square feet or more done inside a negative pressure enclosure, the building owner or lessee must have a post-abatement air monitoring check done by a qualified party independent of the contractor (or, if the owner and contractor agree, by the owner's own staff or the contractor). (4) In apartment buildings and condominiums of 10 or more units, asbestos inspections, response action designs and larger response actions inside the building, other than listed small-scale work, must be done by persons accredited by the state (a certified industrial hygienist may also inspect). (5) Where federal asbestos rules require a notice of intention before renovation or demolition, the owner or operator that files it pays the state a $100 fee. If a lease includes an option to purchase a property of 1 to 4 dwelling units, the seller disclosure statement, which asks whether you know of asbestos and other environmental hazards, must be given before the lease is signed; this library does not cover lease-options. Some cities add rules by ordinance.

title: Pest Control and Fumigation Notices
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to give tenants notice of routine pest control or pesticide applications at a rental property, or to put pest control information in the lease (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched; the state's pesticide use rules may add posting or notice requirements for commercial applications). Three statutes do touch the subject. (1) Anyone who fumigates a building with a gas that is lethal or dangerous to people must lock every entrance for at least 12 hours, post a warning at each entrance that no one may enter without written permission of the sheriff or the local police or fire authorities for at least 48 hours, notify those authorities, and inspect the building at the end of the 48 hours to decide whether it is fit to live in; a violation is a felony and makes the user liable to anyone injured. (2) A business that holds itself out as applying pesticides must hold a commercial applicator license, so hire a licensed applicator. (3) The state keeps a voluntary registry of people with a medically documented condition who must be notified before lawn or ornamental pesticide applications near their homes; it does not cover applications on or within 10 feet of a structure to control pests on that structure. Separate notice rules for schools and day care centers do not apply to housing. Some cities add rules by ordinance.

title: No Portable Cooling Device Rule
bodyText:
No Michigan statute gives a tenant a right to install a window or portable air conditioner, and none requires a landlord to provide air conditioning. Air conditioning you do supply is covered by your repair and habitability covenants. The state residential code does not require a mechanical permit for a portable cooling unit.

The library's `no-alterations` clause requires your written consent for alterations, and a tenant with a disability may still ask for a reasonable accommodation or modification. Some cities set cooling rules by ordinance. An optional clause lets you list the cooling equipment you supply and choose whether tenant-installed units are allowed (`portable-cooling-device-mi`).

title: Wells and Small Water Systems
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to test a private well that serves a single rental home, or to give the tenant well test results (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). It is different if your well or other water system serves 2 or more living units, for example a duplex or a small apartment building on one well. Michigan's Safe Drinking Water Act then treats the system as a public water supply and you as its supplier of water: you must collect water samples on the schedule the state's rules set, have them analyzed by the state laboratory or a certified laboratory and report the results to the state; if the water does not meet state drinking water standards, the state will require you to notify the people you serve of the extent and nature of the problem, in a form it approves; the state may inspect the system; and, if federal drinking water law requires consumer confidence reports for your system, you must give them to customers. A supply that serves at least 15 living units or 25 residents year-round is a community supply, with more duties and annual fees. Well construction is regulated separately. If a lease includes an option to purchase a property of 1 to 4 dwelling units, the seller disclosure statement, which asks about the well and whether the water has been tested, must be given before the lease is signed. Your local health department can advise on testing.

title: Contaminated Property Notice
bodyText:
If you know or have information, or are on notice through a recorded document, that all or part of the parcel is a facility under Part 201 of Michigan's Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act (a place where a hazardous substance is present above the cleanup levels for unrestricted residential use), you may not transfer an interest in the property without first giving written notice of the known general nature and extent of the release and of any land or resource use restrictions you know apply.

A similar rule applies to a site with a release from an underground storage tank under Part 213: written notice that the property is a site and of the general nature and extent of the release, and full disclosure of any land or resource use restrictions that are part of the corrective action.

The statutes do not define a transfer, and a lease conveys an interest in real property, so the cautious course is to give the notice to every tenant in writing before the lease is signed, even where a restrictive covenant or notice is recorded; use `contamination-notice-mi`.

If you own or operate a facility you know about, you must also take due care: prevent the contamination from getting worse, take the response steps needed to prevent unacceptable exposure and allow the intended use safely, take reasonable precautions against foreseeable acts of others (which include tenants), give access to those authorized to carry out the response, and comply with and not impede any land or resource use restrictions.

Michigan has no general environmental covenant act requiring a covenant to be copied to occupants; restrictions are recorded under Part 201 and Part 213.

If a lease includes an option to purchase a property of 1 to 4 dwelling units, the seller disclosure statement, which asks about contaminated soil and other environmental problems, must also be given before signing.

title: No Defective Drywall Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to disclose defective (corrosive or high-sulfur) drywall or to remediate it under a special rule (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). Drywall that damages wiring, plumbing or other systems is a repair and habitability matter under your covenants (`edu-habitability-mi`), and a misleading statement about the property can violate the Consumer Protection Act (`edu-consumer-protection-mi`). Some cities may require more by ordinance.

title: No Chemical Exposure Warning Rule
bodyText: Michigan has no law like California's Proposition 65 that requires warnings to tenants about exposure to chemicals known to cause cancer or reproductive harm, and no statute requiring a formaldehyde notice for rental housing (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). Federal lead-based paint disclosure still applies to most housing built before 1978 (`lead-based-paint`, `edu-lead-hazard-mi`). If a lease includes an option to purchase a property of 1 to 4 dwelling units, the seller disclosure statement, which asks whether urea formaldehyde foam insulation is installed and about asbestos, radon, formaldehyde, lead-based paint and contaminated soil, must be given before the lease is signed; this library does not cover lease-options.

title: No Military or Airport Zone Disclosure Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to tell a tenant that a rental is near a military installation or airport, or inside an aircraft noise zone, accident potential zone or clear zone, and none gives a tenant a right to end the lease on that ground (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). Nothing needs to go in the lease. If you choose to describe aircraft noise or nearby installations, describe them accurately, since a misleading statement can violate the Consumer Protection Act (`edu-consumer-protection-mi`). Local zoning near airports and bases is a local matter not covered here.

title: No Ordnance, Demolition or Meter Disclosure Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to disclose a former military ordnance or munitions location near the property, to tell a prospective tenant that the landlord has applied for or plans a demolition permit, or to disclose before signing that a gas or electric meter serves areas outside the tenant's unit (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, 2025-2026 acts and the Public Service Commission's residential service rules searched). Related rules: where the Housing Law applies, a notice that a building is dangerous, with a hearing on whether to demolish it, goes to the owner, agent or lessee registered with the local enforcing agency (`edu-housing-law-mi`); at least 30 days before shutting off service to a single-metered building used as a residence by 3 or more households for the landlord's unpaid bill, the utility must send a notice to each unit (`edu-utility-landlord-account-mi`); submetering and shared meters are covered in `edu-no-submetering-rule-mi`, and the shared `common-area-lighting-ks` clause covers common-area lights on a tenant's meter.

title: No Shoreline Disclosure Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to tell a tenant about public access along a Great Lakes shoreline, about bottomlands, or that a rental is in a high-risk erosion area, flood risk area or critical dune area (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). Those laws regulate building and land use: the state designates high-risk erosion, flood risk and environmental areas of the Great Lakes shorelands for local zoning or state regulation, and a person may not start a new use in a critical dune area without a permit. They put no lease duty on you. If you describe beach or water access in a listing or lease, describe it accurately (`edu-consumer-protection-mi`). Flood disclosure: `edu-no-flood-disclosure-mi`.

title: Utility Usage Data and Benchmarking
bodyText:
No Michigan statute requires or regulates building energy benchmarking, or gives an owner a right to a tenant's utility usage data.

For electric and natural gas utilities regulated by the Public Service Commission, the Commission's rules require each utility to have an approved customer data privacy policy under which customer usage data and personal information are disclosed to third parties for secondary purposes only with the customer's written consent, and a customer may share his or her own information with a third party. A utility must also give a customer, on request, a statement of the customer's actual or weather-adjusted usage for the last 12 months, and must give weather-adjusted consumption data to the customer or to a third party the customer designates.

So when the account is in the tenant's name, you can get the tenant's usage data only with the tenant's written consent. The shared `energy-data-release-wy` clause, which applies in Michigan as written, gives that consent for benchmarking, audits and efficiency programs, has the tenant sign the utility's own release form on request, and lets the tenant withdraw consent. Municipal and cooperative utilities and water utilities may follow their own policies.

title: No Recycling Notice Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute requires a landlord to provide recycling or to tell tenants where and how to recycle (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution and 2025-2026 acts searched). Michigan's solid waste law sets recycling access standards for counties and municipalities, not landlords: curbside recycling access for at least 90% of single-family dwellings in urban areas by January 1, 2026 and in municipalities of more than 5,000 residents by January 1, 2028, drop-off locations for residents without curbside access by January 1, 2032, and county materials management plans that address expanding convenient recycling access at single and multifamily dwellings. Where the Housing Law applies, the owner of a multiple dwelling must provide proper covered receptacles for garbage, refuse and other waste (`edu-housing-law-mi`). Your city, county or hauler may require recycling at multifamily buildings; local ordinances and contracts are not covered here. Telling tenants where the recycling containers are is good practice.

title: Smoke Drift and Smoke-Free Areas
bodyText:
Michigan has no statute on tobacco or other smoke drifting between units of a residential building.

The Smoke-Free Air Law bans smoking in a public place, which includes a place of employment: an enclosed indoor area containing one or more work areas for people employed by a public or private employer. A leasing office, staff office, maintenance shop or other enclosed area where your employees work is covered, and the owner or manager must post no-smoking signs, remove ashtrays and ask anyone smoking to stop or leave. A residence used as an office only by its owner or lessee is not a place of employment.

Whether an enclosed common hallway becomes a place of employment because your staff clean or maintain it is not settled by the statute's words, so the cautious course is to treat enclosed common areas where employees regularly work as smoke-free. Smoking is also banned in passenger elevators, with a required sign.

You may make the whole property smoke-free by lease, including for marihuana smoking (`smoking-policy-mi`).

The library does not offer a clause in which the tenant gives up claims about drifting smoke: a Michigan lease may not excuse you from liability for failing to perform a duty imposed by law or waive the tenant's remedies when the premises violate the fitness and repair covenants, so such a waiver would likely be void. If smoking is allowed in other units, you may say so accurately.

title: Cure Rights and Eviction Grounds in Michigan
bodyText:
Michigan's eviction statute lists the grounds for recovering possession and gives the tenant a statutory chance to cure in only two cases.

(1) Unpaid rent: you may serve a written demand for possession for nonpayment, and the tenant may stay by paying the rent due within 7 days after service; rent due does not include rent accelerated because of a breach. Instead of a demand, you may end the tenancy for nonpayment with a written 7-day notice to quit; that statute gives no right to pay within the 7 days.

(2) Health hazard or damage: if the person in possession willfully or negligently causes a serious and continuing health hazard, or extensive and continuing physical injury to the premises, that you discovered or should reasonably have discovered no earlier than 90 days before filing, your demand gives the tenant 7 days to deliver possession or substantially restore or repair the premises.

The other statutory grounds carry no cure: holding over after the term ends; after a periodic tenancy or tenancy at will is ended by notice to quit; after the lease is ended under a power to terminate that the lease provides or the law implies; 24 hours after a demand following termination under a controlled-substance clause where a formal police report has been filed; and 7 days after a notice to quit where the tenant, a household member or a person under the tenant's control caused or threatened physical injury to someone on property you own or operate and the police were notified (not where the person injured or threatened was the tenant or a household member, or where it would violate federal housing regulations).

For any other breach of the lease, no Michigan statute gives the tenant a cure period, sets the notice you must give, or says the breached term must be material: your right to end the lease comes from the lease's own termination terms, so the lease may set its own cure period and notice (the library's default clause, `default-by-tenant-mi`, has you give written notice and a number of days you choose to correct a curable breach). Whether a court will end a tenancy over a trivial breach is case law, so give the cure period and end the lease only for a real, documented breach.

A lease cannot shorten the statutory periods or change how a demand is made and served. Every demand must be in writing, addressed to the person in possession, describe the premises, clearly state the reasons and the time to take remedial action, state the amount due if rent or other money is claimed, and be dated and signed by you, your attorney or your agent; serve it by personal delivery, by delivery at the premises to a household member or employee of suitable age and discretion with a request to pass it on, by first-class mail, or electronically only if the tenant gave the specific written consent the statute requires.

A court will not enter a possession judgment where the termination was retaliation, and in a nonpayment case the tenant may show that your breach of the lease excused the rent.

Housing operated by a local government and mobile home parks require just cause. In a condominium, the association must give the unit owner 15 days to correct a tenant's breach of the condominium documents before it may itself sue to evict the tenant.

Federal law also bars requiring a tenant to vacate a property with a federally backed mortgage or in a covered federal housing program until 30 days after a notice to vacate. Local ordinances may add rules; the library does not cover them.

title: Your Remedies When a Michigan Tenant Defaults
bodyText: When a Michigan tenant defaults, you may recover possession and money in one eviction case, or sue for money alone, and choosing one does not give up the other. Possession is recovered by summary proceedings in district court (`edu-eviction-process-mi`, `edu-cure-and-eviction-grounds-mi`). In that case you may join a claim for money damages for wrongful detainer or possession, for breach of the lease, or for waste or malicious destruction of the premises; the tenant may join counterclaims. The money claim may not exceed the court's limit (district court: $25,000), and a larger claim is removed to circuit court. Under the court rules a money claim is dismissed without prejudice, or adjourned if the tenant does not appear, unless the tenant was served with process by personal delivery or restricted certified mail, and the court may try the money claim up to 28 days after the time for issuing the order of eviction runs out if it would delay the possession case or needs the home back first. If the court awards the cost of repairs, your own or your property manager's repair labor is paid at a reasonable rate based on usual and customary charges, as if a third party had done it. A judgment for possession does not merge or bar your other claims: summary proceedings are in addition to every other legal, equitable or statutory remedy, and after winning possession you may sue for damages from the date of your notice to quit or demand for possession. Rent alone may be recovered in an ordinary civil action. The small claims division of the district court hears money claims only, up to $7,000 (since January 1, 2024); it cannot order possession, lawyers may not take part except on their own behalf, both sides give up a jury, a lawyer and any appeal unless one side removes the case to the general civil division, an assignee such as a debt buyer may not file, and a company is represented by an officer or employee who knows the facts (`edu-entity-landlord-court-representation-mi`). Other limits: to keep any part of the security deposit for disputed damages you must sue within 45 days after the occupancy ends, unless the claim is only for unpaid rent or another statutory exception applies (`edu-security-deposit-penalty-mi`); a lease may accelerate rent after a breach only with the statutory statement about your duty to minimize damages, accelerated rent is never rent due for a nonpayment demand, and you must mitigate (`rent-acceleration-mi`, `edu-mitigation-mi`); in the eviction case only the costs the statute allows may be awarded, and a lease cannot shift your attorney fees to the tenant (`edu-attorney-fees-mi`); judgment interest is in `edu-legal-interest-mi`. If the tenant leaves, you may retake possession without a court order only on a good-faith belief, after diligent inquiry, that the tenant has abandoned the home and does not intend to return, with current rent unpaid (`edu-self-help-eviction-mi`). Deadlines for suing are in `edu-limitation-of-actions-mi`. Federal law also bars requiring a tenant to vacate a property with a federally backed mortgage or in a covered federal housing program until 30 days after a notice to vacate (`edu-cares-act-notice`).

title: Tenancies at Will in Michigan
bodyText: In Michigan a tenancy at will, or a tenancy by sufferance, ends when either you or the tenant gives the other 1 month's notice. If rent is payable at intervals shorter than 3 months, notice equal to the interval between rent payments is enough (for monthly rent, one rental period), and the tenancy ends at the end of a period equal to that interval; a notice is not void because the date it names does not fall at the start or end of a rental period. If the tenant does not pay rent, you may instead end the tenancy with a written 7-day notice to quit. A year-to-year tenancy is different: a notice to quit takes effect 1 year after it is served. Give every notice in writing and keep proof of service: if the tenant stays after the notice ends the tenancy, you recover possession through summary proceedings, and the court rules require a copy of the notice, showing when and how it was served, attached to your complaint (`edu-termination-notice-mi`, `edu-eviction-process-mi`). You may not lock the tenant out (`edu-self-help-eviction-mi`), and a court will not enter possession if the notice was retaliation (`edu-retaliation-mi`). Michigan's statutes do not define a tenancy at will or say how one is created; whether a particular arrangement (for example, a stay while a lease is negotiated, an occupant who pays no fixed rent, or a tenant under a lease that fails for lack of a writing) is at will, periodic or by sufferance is case law. The label rarely changes the notice, since the same statute sets the notice for estates at will and by sufferance and measures it by the rent interval. A lease for longer than 1 year is void unless it, or a note or memorandum of it, is in writing and signed by the landlord or an agent authorized in writing; a lease of 1 year or less need not be in writing (`edu-statute-of-frauds-mi`). Put any informal arrangement in writing with its rent, rent interval and notice terms. A fixed-term lease ends at the end of its term without notice unless the lease requires one; for a tenant who stays on, see `edu-holdover-mi`. Federal law also bars requiring a tenant to vacate a property with a federally backed mortgage or in a covered federal housing program until 30 days after a notice to vacate (`edu-cares-act-notice`).

title: Saving a Michigan Tenancy From Forfeiture
bodyText: A Michigan tenant can save the tenancy from forfeiture only in the ways the eviction statute provides. Before you file: for unpaid rent, the tenant keeps the tenancy by paying the rent due within 7 days after you serve a demand for possession; for a serious and continuing health hazard or extensive and continuing damage, by substantially restoring or repairing the premises within 7 days after your demand. The other grounds for ending a tenancy (end of term, notice to quit, a power to terminate in the lease, the controlled-substance and physical-injury grounds) give no statutory chance to cure (`edu-cure-and-eviction-grounds-mi`). After judgment: if you won possession because money due under the tenancy was not paid, the judgment states the amount due at trial, after deducting any rent excused by your breach of the lease or of your repair covenants, and the order of eviction may not issue if the tenant pays that amount with the taxed costs within the time the judgment allows; in most cases the order cannot issue until 10 days after judgment (`edu-redemption-mi`). A possession judgment on any other ground carries no such right. No Michigan statute lets a court relieve a residential tenant from forfeiture on other terms; whether a court could still grant equitable relief is case law. The statute's equitable right of redemption belongs to a land contract buyer, not a tenant. Your own conduct can undo a forfeiture. The Court of Appeals has held that a landlord who habitually accepted late rent must first tell the tenant that strict compliance with the due date will be required before ending the tenancy for late payment, and that accepting rent for a period after the date in a notice to quit, before the tenant knew of the eviction case, waived the notice (`edu-acceptance-of-payment-mi`). Under the court rules, paying or accepting money before trial does not necessarily stop the case, and after judgment you may not get the order of eviction once any part of the judgment amount is paid unless a hearing is held or the judgment says partial payment will not prevent it. A lease cannot take away these rights or change the eviction procedure. Federal law also bars requiring a tenant to vacate a property with a federally backed mortgage or in a covered federal housing program until 30 days after a notice to vacate (`edu-cares-act-notice`).

title: Paying to Stop a Michigan Eviction
bodyText: Michigan gives a tenant behind on rent three chances to pay and keep the home. (1) Within 7 days after you serve a demand for possession for nonpayment, by paying the rent due (`edu-nonpayment-notice-mi`). (2) During the case: in a nonpayment case under a residential lease, the court must tell the tenant at the first hearing that the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services, a local Coordinated Entry Agency or Housing Assessment and Resource Agency, or the federal Help for Homeless Veterans program may help pay the rent; that the summons and complaint are enough to apply, with no judgment needed; and about community dispute resolution and conditional dismissal. If the tenant gives the court written proof of an application within 5 days, the court must stay the case for 14 days, longer if the application is still pending or approved, but never more than 28 days in all. Under the court rules, paying or accepting money before trial does not necessarily stop or delay the case. (3) After judgment: the judgment states the amount due at trial, after deducting any rent excused by your breach of the lease or repair covenants, and when and on what conditions an order of eviction will issue. If the tenant pays that amount with the taxed costs within the time allowed, the order of eviction may not issue; in most cases it cannot issue until 10 days after judgment. When you apply for the order you must show any money accepted after judgment and on what conditions, and once any part of the judgment amount has been paid the order may not issue unless a hearing is held or the judgment itself says partial payment will not prevent it. The order must issue within 56 days after judgment and be carried out within 56 days after it issues unless a hearing is held. Michigan prescribes no wording for accepting a partial payment while keeping your rights; if you will accept part payments after judgment, ask for a judgment that says they will not prevent the order. No Michigan statute makes you accept rent from a charity or other third party or regulates how such a payment is made, but if you and related entities own 5 or more rental units in Michigan you may not set different terms for a tenant because the tenant uses emergency rental assistance or other lawful income (`edu-source-of-income-mi`); if you participate in the state's rent vendoring program you may not evict a tenant based solely on the state ending your participation over a housing code hazard or unpaid property taxes; and your lease must allow at least one fee-free way to pay rent (`acceptable-payment-methods-mi`). Federal law also bars requiring a tenant to vacate a property with a federally backed mortgage or in a covered federal housing program until 30 days after a notice to vacate (`edu-cares-act-notice`).

title: Bonds and Escrow in a Michigan Eviction
bodyText: Michigan has no possession bond that a tenant gives at signing to secure delivery of the home at the end of the term, and no bond you must post to start an eviction. A lease may not provide for a confession of judgment, so a term in which the tenant agrees in advance to a judgment for possession is void (`edu-truth-in-renting-mi`). The bonds and escrow payments that do exist are set by the eviction statute and the court rules, and most fall on the tenant once the case is under way: (1) Escrow before trial: if trial is adjourned more than 14 days and you show a clear need for protection, the court may order the tenant to pay a reasonable rent into court, taking account of the condition of the premises; only the court may release it, and a tenant who does not pay loses the right to a jury on possession and you get a trial within 14 days (`edu-eviction-process-mi`). (2) Motions after judgment: a motion challenging a possession judgment must be filed within 10 days, and the court may not stay the judgment unless the motion comes with an escrow deposit of 1 month's rent or the court waives the deposit because there are grounds for relief from the judgment; a hearing follows within 14 days. (3) Appeals: either side may appeal within 10 days. A tenant who appeals must file a bond covering the appeal costs, the amount due stated in the judgment and your damages from the date of the notice to quit or demand for possession, and the court must order the tenant to pay into escrow while the appeal is pending; a tenant who cannot get sureties or make a cash deposit may comply with an escrow order instead. A landlord who appeals files a bond for the appeal costs only. An appeal or a motion for a new trial filed, with a bond to stay proceedings, before the order of eviction may issue suspends the time for issuing it until the appeal or motion is decided, and a claim of appeal with a bond or escrow order stays an order of eviction that has been issued but not carried out. Fees for carrying out an order of eviction must be reasonable, and a party may object to them by motion. Local ordinances may add rules; the library does not cover them.

title: Who Receives Eviction Papers for Your Tenant
bodyText: No Michigan statute lets your lease name a person to receive eviction notices or court papers for your tenant, and the library offers no such clause. Your demand for possession or notice to quit goes to the person in possession: by personal delivery; by delivery at the premises to a member of the household or an employee of suitable age and discretion, asking that it be passed on; by first-class mail (served on the next regular mail delivery day); or electronically only if the tenant has given specific written consent to electronic service and the consent was confirmed by electronic reply (`electronic-service-consent-mi`). You may not refuse to lease to someone who declines electronic service. The summons and complaint must be mailed to the tenant and also served in one of three ways under the court rules: by a method of the general service rule (such as personal delivery or certified mail restricted to the tenant); by delivery at the premises to a household member of suitable age who is told what the papers are and asked to deliver them; or, after diligent attempts at personal service, by securely attaching them to the main entrance of the tenant's home. A default for a residential tenant who does not appear generally requires personal service or, with other service, a second copy mailed by the court in a court envelope (`edu-eviction-process-mi`). A statute and the court rules allow service of process on an agent authorized by written appointment to receive it, but no Michigan text says a lease term can make that appointment for eviction cases, and a lease term that alters a right of notice or procedure in a court case under the lease, or requires the tenant to give you a power of attorney, is void (`edu-truth-in-renting-mi`). Serve the tenant directly. One statute names a substitute. A tenant enrolled in Michigan's Address Confidentiality Program (for victims of domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking or sexual assault) has designated the Department of Technology, Management, and Budget as agent to receive mail and service of process; the department forwards process by certified mail. If you ask, the department or the Attorney General will confirm only whether the person is a participant and, once process is forwarded, the date it was mailed. The act does not say whether serving the department replaces service at the rental, so if you learn your tenant is a participant, serve the department as well as serving by a court-rule method at the property. Your own side is different: the lease must state the name and address where notices to you are given (`lessor-notice-address-mi`).

title: No Cold-Weather Move-Out Notice Rule
bodyText: No Michigan statute or administrative rule requires your tenant to tell you before moving out of, or leaving empty, a home with pipes that can freeze, sets a winter window for such a notice, or makes leaving without one an offense (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, administrative rules and 2025-2026 acts searched). If you want that protection it has to come from the lease. The library's optional heat and freeze protection clause has the tenant keep the heat at a minimum you set whenever pipes could freeze, tell you before an absence of more than a number of days you choose, and pay the actual cost of freeze damage caused by the tenant's deliberate, negligent or irresponsible failure, while leaving heating repairs with you; the optional absence-notice clause asks for notice of any absence of more than 7 days (`extended-absence-notice-ks`). Without such a term, a tenant who damages the home through wilful or irresponsible conduct or lack of conduct, such as shutting off the heat in winter, is responsible for that disrepair under the repair covenant's own exception (`tenant-caused-damage-mi`), and you keep your duty to keep the home fit and in reasonable repair, including the heat (`edu-habitability-mi`). If a tenant seems to have left, you may retake possession without a court order only if you believe in good faith, after diligent inquiry, that the tenant has abandoned the home and does not intend to return, and current rent is unpaid (`abandoned-property-mi`); you may enter at any time in an emergency such as a flood, and otherwise as the lease's entry terms allow (`landlords-access-mi`). Local ordinances may add rules; the library does not cover them.

title: No Defense for Late Benefit Payments
bodyText: No Michigan statute gives a tenant a defense, a continuance or a right to reinstatement because a Social Security payment, another government benefit or a rental-assistance payment arrives late. The ordinary rules apply: the tenant may pay within 7 days after your demand for possession, the court must pause a residential nonpayment case for up to 28 days while a rental-assistance application is pending, and after judgment the tenant may pay the judgment amount and costs to stop the eviction (`edu-redemption-mi`). Three rules protect assisted tenants. (1) State rent vendoring: if you take part in the state's rent vendoring program and the state ends your participation because of a housing code hazard or unpaid property taxes, you may not evict the tenant based solely on that; a tenant evicted in violation may recover three times the damages, costs and attorney fees. If the state refuses to pay public-assistance rent because a building official found code violations through your fault, you may not sue that tenant for rent or possession while the refusal lasts (`edu-rent-demand-bar-mi`). (2) Housing Choice Vouchers (federal): the family does not owe the part of the rent the housing agency's payment covers, the agency's failure to pay you is not a breach of the lease by the tenant, and during the lease term you may not end the tenancy because the agency's payment is late or missing. Pursue the agency under your contract with it, and evict only for the tenant's own share. (3) Source of income: if you and related entities own 5 or more rental units in Michigan, you may not deny or end a tenancy, or set different terms, because of a tenant's lawful source of income, such as Social Security, supplemental security income, public assistance or a voucher, or because the tenant uses emergency rental assistance (`edu-source-of-income-mi`); a lease term that applies only to assisted tenants risks that rule. Federal law also bars requiring a tenant to vacate a property with a federally backed mortgage or in a covered federal housing program until 30 days after a notice to vacate (`edu-cares-act-notice`).

title: When Your Tenant Files for Bankruptcy
bodyText: Michigan's statutes say nothing about evicting a tenant who has filed for bankruptcy, so federal bankruptcy law controls. The filing creates an automatic stay that generally stops you from starting or continuing an eviction case, enforcing a judgment, or taking any act to obtain possession of property of the bankruptcy estate, which includes the tenant's lease. Two federal exceptions matter. (1) A judgment for possession you obtained before the tenant filed: the stay does not stop you from continuing the eviction. But Michigan law lets a tenant stop the order of eviction after a nonpayment judgment by paying the judgment amount and costs within the time allowed (`edu-redemption-mi`), so a tenant may file with the bankruptcy petition a certification that state law allows a cure after judgment and deposit with the bankruptcy clerk the rent for the 30 days after filing; the exception is then delayed 30 days, and if within those 30 days the tenant certifies having cured the entire money default, the exception does not apply unless the court rules for you on an objection (the court holds a hearing within 10 days). If the tenant lists your judgment on the petition but files no certification, the exception applies at once. Whether the exception also frees the court case itself is bankruptcy case law, so confirm with bankruptcy counsel before the next step. (2) An eviction based on endangering the property or illegal use of controlled substances there: the stay stops applying 15 days after you file and serve a certification, under penalty of perjury, that you have filed the eviction or that the tenant did so in the previous 30 days, unless the tenant objects and shows the court the situation did not exist or has been remedied. In any other case, ask the bankruptcy court for relief from the stay before you serve a demand, file, or ask for an order of eviction. Under Michigan's court rules a party who is a debtor must file and serve notice of the bankruptcy in the eviction case within 3 days, you may file the notice if the tenant does not, and the court may hold the case in abeyance until the stay no longer applies. In a chapter 7 case a residential lease the trustee does not assume within 60 days after the order for relief (or a longer time the court sets within that period) is deemed rejected; in other chapters it may be assumed or rejected up to plan confirmation. A lease in default can be assumed only if the default is cured or adequately assured, you are compensated for your actual loss, and future performance is adequately assured. A lease term ending the tenancy because the tenant is insolvent or files for bankruptcy cannot be enforced after the case begins. Get bankruptcy advice before acting.

title: Delays and Stays in a Michigan Eviction
bodyText: Michigan has no eviction moratorium and no statute that lets a court postpone an eviction because of a tenant's hardship, illness, age or children, the weather or season, or holidays (Michigan Compiled Laws, Constitution, court rules and 2025-2026 acts searched). The delays that exist come from the eviction statute, the court rules and federal law. Rental assistance: in a nonpayment case under a residential lease, the court must stay the case if the tenant gives written proof, within 5 days after being told of the right, of an application for rental assistance to the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services, a local Coordinated Entry Agency or Housing Assessment and Resource Agency, or the federal Help for Homeless Veterans program; the stay ends after 14 days unless the application is still pending or approved, and never lasts more than 28 days (`edu-redemption-mi`). Adjournments: at the first hearing the court generally adjourns trial for 7 to 14 days; for good cause it may adjourn up to 56 days, and if it adjourns more than 14 days it may order the tenant to pay rent into court (`edu-possession-bond-mi`). A consent judgment entered when either side has no lawyer cannot be enforced for 3 court business days, and an unrepresented party may move to set it aside in that time. After judgment: the order of eviction generally cannot issue until 10 days after judgment (immediately in listed cases, such as a controlled-substance termination, trespass or a serious health hazard), must be issued within 56 days after judgment and carried out within 56 days after it issues unless a hearing is held, and only a court officer, bailiff, sheriff or local police officer may carry it out (`edu-eviction-process-mi`). A tenant who appeals or moves for relief within 10 days gets a stay only with a bond or escrow deposit, or a court order waiving it (`edu-possession-bond-mi`). Federal stays: a tenant's bankruptcy filing (`edu-tenant-bankruptcy-mi`); and for a servicemember or dependents, an eviction from a home with rent up to an inflation-adjusted limit needs a court order, and the court may on its own and must on the servicemember's request, where military service materially affects the ability to pay, stay the case for 90 days (or longer or shorter as justice requires) or adjust the lease (`edu-no-servicemember-statute-mi`); no Michigan statute adds a state military eviction stay. Local governments: no Michigan statute was found either authorizing or forbidding a local eviction moratorium; check your city's ordinances, which the library does not cover. Federal law also bars requiring a tenant to vacate a property with a federally backed mortgage or in a covered federal housing program until 30 days after a notice to vacate (`edu-cares-act-notice`).

title: Minors as Tenants and Eviction Defendants
bodyText: In Michigan a person is an adult for all purposes at 18; there is no higher age for signing a lease. A minor who is emancipated has an adult's rights, expressly including the right to enter into enforceable contracts such as apartment leases and to sue and be sued. Emancipation happens by operation of law when the minor is on active duty with the U.S. armed forces or was validly emancipated under another state's law, and otherwise by order of the family division of circuit court; ask for proof.
